rule: Budgets are fixed before measuring and never adjusted after results. A missing measurement is not a pass. Speedups must keep output byte-identical.

laptop.machine: MacBook Pro M5 Max, quiet (load1 < 2.0, no foreign build or benchmark)

workload.description: warm daemon v2 session, 12-turn EN/DE history (~32 KiB), new message with PII sized uniformly 512-4096 bytes, gaze setup policy written by the binary itself, strict restore. Cold start: spawn to first validated clean with a warm page cache, at least 5 runs, maximum reported.

server.machine: Amp orb a1.medium: 4 vCPU (shared, not dedicated), 8 GB, x86-64 Linux, x86-64 release binary built in the orb. Replaces the originally decided Hetzner CCX23 (4 dedicated vCPU, 16 GB, Debian 13), which was not rented. Same architecture, OS family and vCPU count; half the memory, still over 3x the 2.5 GB peak budget. Shared vCPUs make it at most as fast and noisier than a CCX23, so a pass here is conservative; budget numbers are unchanged.

workload.description: as laptop, with 4 sessions on one resident daemon; each step sends the 4 sessions' frames as one simultaneous burst, so per-turn latency includes queueing behind the other sessions
